content.value_statement: Reusable AI workflows are hard to write consistently. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through designing, writing, and refining slash commands.
actual_capabilities: Selects project-level or global command locations from repository context and user preference.
Explains workflow, CI fixing, agent delegation, and simple execution command patterns.
Collects command name, arguments, workflow steps, tools, and error handling requirements.
Generates frontmatter and agent-executable markdown instructions for slash commands.
Creates command files under .claude/commands or ~/.claude/commands when requested.
Uses bundled examples and best practices to improve command quality.
limitations: It does not execute the generated slash command automatically.
It needs clear workflow details from the user before writing useful commands.
Generated commands may run shell tools when the requested workflow requires them.
Claude Code slash command behavior can vary by environment and permissions.

use_cases.title: Automate Project Workflows
use_cases.description: Create project commands for reviews, test fixes, pull requests, and repeatable repository tasks.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Procedures
use_cases.description: Turn shared release, review, and validation steps into consistent commands for a repository.

use_cases.title: Build Personal Commands
use_cases.description: Create global commands for common personal workflows across many projects.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Command
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a slash command named <name> that helps me with <task>. Ask for missing details before writing it.

prompt_templates.title: Add Arguments and Scope
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a project-level slash command for <workflow>. It should accept <arguments> and explain failures clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize a Team Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Turn our <process> steps into a reusable slash command. Include success criteria, error handling, and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Iterative Automation
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an advanced command that runs <checks>, fixes safe issues, repeats until success, and stops after clear limits.

output_examples.input: Create a command that runs project validation and reports failures.
output_examples.output: A project command with a clear name, short description, validation steps, failure reporting, and stop conditions.

output_examples.input: Make a global command for my recurring review workflow.
output_examples.output: A global command file with argument guidance, review steps, tool notes, and a concise completion summary.

output_examples.input: Create a command that prepares a pull request stack.
output_examples.output: A workflow command that checks context, prepares commits, submits the stack, and reports created pull requests.

best_practices: Confirm project or global scope before writing a command file.
Define command inputs, success criteria, and error handling before generation.
Review generated commands before using them on important repositories.
anti_patterns: Creating commands with vague steps that require interpretation during execution.
Writing global commands when the workflow only applies to one repository.
Embedding destructive shell operations without explicit user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates Claude Code slash command files that expand into reusable workflow prompts.

faq.question: Where are command files stored?
faq.answer: Project commands use .claude/commands. Global commands use ~/.claude/commands.

faq.question: Can it create commands with arguments?
faq.answer: Yes. It can add argument hints and explain required or optional inputs.

faq.question: Does it run the generated command?
faq.answer: No. It writes the command and explains how to invoke it.

faq.question: Can it use examples from the skill package?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples and best practices for common command patterns.

faq.question: Is it only for coding workflows?
faq.answer: It is focused on Claude Code, but commands can describe many repeatable developer workflows.
